newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold, silver likely to head down further.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold, silver likely to head down further.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold will probably sink further to test support at the February 12 low of $336.15 after it breached important resistance at $340 on Monday, technical analysts said.
Silver tumbled through the key $4.70 level and was now likely to head lower to search for support, possibly around the $4.50 area. Platinum could cling to $370.
GOLD -- Gold's upside potential evaporated on Monday after it breached key support at $340 following the expiry of over-the-counter options which had helped it hold that level for the past week.
Although bullion recovered from a session low of $338.70 an ounce in late trading, analysts said a slide to the February 12 low of $336.15 remained a potential threat.
"While it's below $345, $336.15 looks very much under pressure," said Karen Jones, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston. "If that doesn't hold there is not a lot between there and $325.10."
The $325.10 level, which Jones said was "quite feasible" coincides with the low from March 1993.
Gold's prospects would improve however if it could resurface above the rock-solid resistance of $345, which was highly unlikely at this stage.
The market's fortunes were battered across the precious metals complex on Monday as prices sank in a move spreadheaded by silver.
Some traders said aside from the dollar's relentless rise, the market was also pressured by rumours that Russia would settle a Swiss debt by supplying platinum and palladium against a gold swap.
By 0810 GMT bullion was quoted at $339.10/39.50 an ounce compared with New York's close of $339.45/39.95.
SILVER - The gloomiest picture in the precious metals complex emerged in silver after it broke below the important $4.70 support on Monday, touching a two-year low of $4.59 in late session.
There was little intervention down from $4.62, the low from January as the market broke below its consolidation phase.
Karen Jones, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, said a 20-point measurement from the bottom of silver's range of $4.65 would take the market down to $4.45.
"At $4.45 there is not much support apart from the actual measurement. I think we are now looking towards the low of 4.33 from March 1995," said Jones.
"I think it will now struggle to regain $4.70," she added.
The gold/silver ratio was likely to rise to around 76 from 73.50 on Monday, Jones said.
By 0810 GMT silver stood at $4.63/$4.65 an ounce after New York's close of $4.62/$4.64.
PLATINUM - The $370 support level was expected to hold for now although the market could struggle to recapture $375-$380, analysts said.
"Further sideways consolidation is going to be likely," said Jones. "If it doesn't hold $370, there's not a lot until $360. So $370 is quite a key support."
She said the platinum/gold ratio looked toppy at 32 and could head back towards 24.
By 0810 GMT platinum stood at $372.25/3.25 an ounce compared with $372.00/$373.00 on Monday.
--Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
